messages:
carla_support: Customer on paid plan reports 401 from hosted API only after building Next.js app with Turbopack. Works in dev (next dev) but prod build strips Authorization header on runtime requests. They say "works when importing from node_modules directly, fails when bundled". Repro steps below and package.json export map. Can eng help triage?

carla_support: Repro steps (condensed):
1) npx create-next-app@latest --ts
2) pnpm add @redwood/sdk@2.3.0
3) add server-side route that calls client: const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY }); await c.generate(...);
4) build with Turbopack (next build) and deploy to Vercel. Runtime requests return 401. Local dev (next dev) is fine.

carla_support: package.json snippet from the app:
```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk": "2.3.0"
  },
  "type": "module"
}
```

carla_support: package.json from node_modules/@redwood/sdk:@redwood/sdk/package.json:
```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/sdk",
  "version": "2.3.0",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.esm.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "import": "./dist/index.esm.js",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js",
      "default": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
    }
  }
}
```

carla_support: Observed behaviour: network inspector on serverless shows outgoing request to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with no Authorization header. Upstream returns 401. Customer says if they directly `import client from '../node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.cjs.js'` in their code the header is present and calls succeed.

sam_eng: Hmm. My first guess: bundler is resolving the ESM entry and doing some tree-shaking or inlining that ends up dropping runtime header attach step (maybe due to conditional side-effect ordering). Turbopack has been known to aggressively optimize.

sam_eng: A few quick asks: can you grab the built server bundle (server/.next/ or .vercel/output) and grep for RW_KEY or Authorization? Also confirm whether this is happening in a Node SSR runtime or Edge function. Edge has different fetch semantics and sometimes strips custom headers.

carla_support: Customer confirmed this is Node SSR (server runtime) not edge. They inspected bundle and couldn't find the code path that sets headers (we might be buried behind small helper that bundler removed).

mikayla_devx: Workarounds to try for customer while we triage:
- Import the CJS entry explicitly as a temporary patch: `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk/dist/index.cjs.js'`
- Pin bundler to avoid ESM optimization: set `experimental.turbopack: false` in next.config.js for now
- Add `"exports": {"node": "./dist/index.cjs.js"}` to their local package resolution via patch-package (ugly but quick)

mikayla_devx: Also note: some bundlers prefer a `node` condition in exports. If they only provide `import`/`require` our `import` may be picked and behave differently. Adding `"node"` condition that points to CJS can force Node same-as-local behavior.

jordan_repro: I whipped up a super-minimal repro (server SSR) that reproduces the missing header when built with Turbopack: https://gist.github.com/jordan-repro/abcdef123456 (private gist). Steps + minimal repo in gist, includes built bundle diff showing our header helper missing.

sam_eng: Thanks @jordan_repro — can you attach a diff of the transpiled files (pre-build vs post-build) showing where our header setter function disappears? That will help packaging team.

sam_eng: If this is a conditional-exports bug (resolver picks ESM entry in an environment we expect CJS), packaging team should add an explicit `node` condition and make CJS the default for Node runtime until we audit ESM behavior.

carla_support: Customer is blocked in prod. Escalating to eng-packaging + eng-platform for priority fix and an immediate support workaround. I told customer we have a workaround and asked if they can apply patch-package or explicit import for now.

deploy-bot: Created issue PACK-894 (eng-packaging) with reproduction and customer logs — assignee: @sam_eng, priority: P1, link: https://go.redwood/issue/PACK-894 :construction:
